Test equal indirect effects across the two levels of a native two-level fit

Source: R/sem-twolevel-equal-indirect.R
twolevel_equal_indirect.Rd

Likelihood-ratio test of the null that the within-level and the between-level indirect effects are equal, \(a_w b_w = a_b b_b\), for a native two-level fit from fit_sem() with cluster =. The statistic is the free fit's likelihood against the fit with that one nonlinear equality. It is a separate test: the descriptive within-minus-between contrast of nie(level = "contrast") is never reported by nie() with a p-value, and there is no Wald test of it here.

Usage

twolevel_equal_indirect(
  object,
  a_within = "a_w",
  b_within = "b_w",
  a_between = "a_b",
  b_between = "b_b",
  n_starts = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  n_boot = 0L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A SEMFit from fit_sem() with cluster = (a two-level model).

a_within, b_within

The labels of the within-level (level 1) a and b regression paths.

a_between, b_between

The labels of the between-level (level 2) a and b regression paths.

n_starts, control

Optimizer settings for the constrained refit; NULL keeps the fit's own.

n_boot

Number of parametric bootstrap replications of the statistic (default 0, none). Each replication draws clustered data of the same cluster sizes from the constrained fit, refits both models and keeps the statistic; replications that do not resolve (an inadmissible, non-positive-definite or non-converged refit) are dropped, so the bootstrap p-value is conditional on admissible refits, and the number dropped is reported (boot$n_dropped). The bootstrap p-value is (1 + #{LR* >= LR}) / (n_valid + 1); use it at a small number of clusters, where the between-level asymptotics are poor.

seed

Optional integer seed for the bootstrap; the caller's random number state is restored.

Value

An object of class c("twolevel_equal_indirect", "htest"): statistic (LR, the scale of mbco_sem()), parameter (df = 1), p.value (chi-square(1)), method, data.name, n_obs, n_clusters, level (c("within", "between")), indirect (the two indirect effects of the free fit and of the constrained fit), unresolved, note, near_singular, twin, and boot (NULL, or a list with statistic, p.value, n_boot, n_valid and n_dropped when n_boot > 0). twin records what the twin certificate did, for resolved and unresolved results: tried (a twin refit was attempted), replaced (a twin replaced the kept fit), flipped (read from the signs of the adopted fit's four path estimates against the kept fit's, not from the start that produced it: "within" or "between" when both paths of that pair changed sign, "other" once for any other sign change, including a path that reaches or leaves zero, and empty when no sign changed, as when the twin is another optimum in the kept fit's sign pattern), f_gain (the kept discrepancy minus the adopted one, 0 if none; the statistic drops by n_obs * f_gain) and unresolved (a better inadmissible or covariance-stage twin made the result unresolved). print() does not show it.

Details

The null a_w b_w = a_b b_b is a smooth surface except where all four paths are 0, where it is singular. Away from that point the likelihood-ratio statistic is referred to chi-square(1), an asymptotic law in the number of clusters J (the between-level paths rest on J clusters). Near it, and when a level-2 variance is near the boundary, the chi-square(1) law may not hold; no closed-form law is claimed. The function warns when all four free-fit paths are within two standard errors of 0 (class medfit_warning_twolevel_equal_singular) and when a level-2 variance at the constrained fit is below 1% of its implied between plus within variance.

The constrained surface has sign twins: flipping the signs of the within pair \((a_w, b_w)\), the between pair \((a_b, b_b)\) or both leaves the equality satisfied, at a worse likelihood. The optimizer's "the starts disagree" warning is not raised when every disagreeing accepted start is such a twin of the kept fit; the lowest-discrepancy start is kept. Any other disagreement among the starts, and every other optimizer warning, is signaled as usual.

After the refit the pair-sign twins of the kept fit are tried as well (a twin certificate): each flip of a pair with no zero is fitted once from the kept estimates with that flip, and the lowest discrepancy is kept. It is a local search of up to three single-start solves, not a proof of a global optimum: a twin refit that fails is skipped, and the search runs at every n_starts, so a worse twin is not kept with n_starts = 1, where no second start is compared. It changes the statistic only when a twin ends lower. A twin that ends at an inadmissible solution (a level-2 variance on its boundary) or with a covariance matrix that is not positive definite, below the kept discrepancy, makes the result unresolved, as it does with more starts. When the better optimum has a level-2 variance on its boundary the result is therefore unresolved or, with n_starts = 1 in very small samples (about 12 clusters), a non-global optimum, as before the certificate. The row allows eight sign patterns; flipping pairs together reaches the four of the kept fit's orbit. The other orbit does hold local optima: a per-elimination oracle found local optima in both orbits in 30 of 35 small cells (closest gap 0.02 LR). The kept orbit still won every time that was tested (no win from the other orbit in 84 stress cells, 114 QA cells with an all-orthant oracle and 715 constrained fits from signed starts), so the coverage of the other orbit rests on the free-fit-pattern and all-positive default starts: evidence, not a proof. The pair flip is a symmetry of the constraint, not of the likelihood, so the twins are separate local optima. Cost: a call takes about 3 to 4 times as long at n_starts = 1, about twice at the default and about 1.3 times at 30 starts; a bootstrap replicate costs about 2.5 times the engine fits.

The guard admits the equality of any two a-then-b chains with the same x, m and y at levels 1 and 2, so a serial a*d or d*b chain of the same shape is admitted too; only the a*b indirect effect of a single mediator has an oracle and a gate here.

The constrained fit is never trusted blindly: if it ends at an inadmissible solution (a negative variance at either level, a covariance matrix that is not positive definite, class medfit_warning_twolevel_inadmissible), does not converge, or has a lower discrepancy than the free fit, the result is unresolved (statistic and p.value NA, unresolved = TRUE, the reason in note) with a warning, never a likelihood-ratio number. If the fit already carries a nonlinear constraint, or the four paths are not the level-1 and level-2 regressions, the call is refused with class medfit_error_twolevel_unsupported; a single-level fit is medfit_error_twolevel_required.

See also

mbco_sem(), fit_sem(), nie()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
id <- rep(1:40, each = 6)
x <- stats::rnorm(40)[id] + stats::rnorm(240)
m <- 0.5 * x + stats::rnorm(40)[id] + stats::rnorm(240)
y <- 0.4 * m + 0.2 * x + stats::rnorm(40)[id] + stats::rnorm(240)
d <- data.frame(cluster = id, X = x, M = m, Y = y)
fit <- fit_sem(
  "level: 1\n M ~ a_w*X\n Y ~ b_w*M + X\nlevel: 2\n M ~ a_b*X\n Y ~ b_b*M + X",
  data = d, cluster = "cluster"
)
twolevel_equal_indirect(fit)
#> 
#> 	Likelihood-ratio test of equal indirect effects across the two levels
#> 
#> data:  a_w * b_w == a_b * b_b
#> LR = 0.30061, df = 1, p-value = 0.5835
#> 
#> 
#> Within vs between indirect effect: free fit 0.2095 vs 0.2978; clusters = 40
# }
